name: Nerello Mascalese

lines.s10: Nerello Mascalese is the red of Mount Etna, pale as a Pinot Noir, with sour cherry, blood orange and a smoky edge.
lines.s20: Nerello Mascalese grows on the black lava slopes of Mount Etna in Sicily, often from old bush vines. It pours pale, with sour cherry, wild strawberry and blood orange, and grips with high acidity and a fine, dusty tannin.
lines.s45: Nerello Mascalese climbs Mount Etna on terraces of black lava, past a thousand metres above the Sicilian sea. Many of the vines are old bushes, never grafted. It looks pale, like a Pinot Noir, and tastes of sour cherry, wild strawberry and blood orange, with a smoky, ashy edge. The acidity is high and the tannin fine but firm. Most is aged gently, often in large old casks, so the place speaks louder than the wood. Pour it with grilled tuna, wild mushrooms or roast lamb. DNA has shown that one of its parents is Sangiovese, the grape of Chianti.
lines.sale: Nerello Mascalese has the perfume of a Pinot Noir and the grip of a Nebbiolo, with a smoky edge from the volcano. Pour it a shade cool beside the grilled tuna or the mushrooms.

glass.lead: Sour cherry, wild strawberry and blood orange with rose and volcanic ash, pale garnet, on high acidity and a fine, dusty tannin.

ladder.where: The high north slope of Etna, from Randazzo to Castiglione di Sicilia
Etna's lower south east slope and the hills of Faro

glass.structure: Dry. Acidity high, tannin medium plus, fine and dusty, alcohol medium, body medium; pale garnet, often translucent.

home.home: Mount Etna in Sicily, on terraces of black lava from about 400 to over 1,000 metres, with many old bush vines on their own roots. Etna Rosso is at least 80 per cent Nerello Mascalese, often aged in large old casks, and may name its contrada. Faro, above Messina, is its other home.
home.abroad: It hardly leaves Sicily: a little grows across the strait in Calabria, and almost nowhere else.

service.temp: 59 to 63 degrees Fahrenheit, 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; a young bottle at the cool end.
service.glass: A wide Burgundy bowl, to gather the rose and red cherry perfume.
service.decant: Consider it for a young contrada wine after a taste; it opens much as a Nebbiolo does.
service.age: Five to fifteen years for Etna Rosso from a named contrada; simpler bottles usually within five.

with.why: fine tannin and high acidity suit a meaty fish

with.dish: Wild mushrooms or a mushroom risotto
with.why: smoke and dried thyme meet the mushrooms' depth
acidity and a firm grip cut the fat
sour cherry and acidity lift the rich meat

labels.means: At least 80 per cent Nerello Mascalese, with Nerello Cappuccio up to a fifth, from the slopes of Etna.
A named district of Etna, often one lava flow of one age, printed on the label like a cru.
The darker, softer partner grape, allowed to a fifth of Etna Rosso for colour and flesh.
A red led by Nerello Mascalese from the hills above Messina, at Sicily's north eastern tip.
A rosé, and a sparkling wine made in the bottle, both from Nerello Mascalese.

guest.q: It is so pale. Is it a light wine?
guest.a: Pale, but not slight. Nerello Mascalese carries little colour, yet high acidity and a fine, firm tannin give it a grip much like a Nebbiolo or a mountain Pinot Noir.

guest.q: Does the volcano change the taste?
guest.a: Many tasters find a smoky, ashy edge. The height matters as much: vineyards up to over 1,000 metres give cool nights, a late harvest and bright acidity.

guest.q: What does contrada mean on the label?
guest.a: A named district on the slopes of Etna, often one lava flow of one age, so it works much like a cru in Burgundy.

compare.tell: Pinot Noir is silkier, with forest floor and softer tannin; Nerello Mascalese has a firmer, dustier grip, with blood orange and volcanic ash.
Nebbiolo has tar and a fiercer, drying tannin; Nerello Mascalese is gentler in grip, with blood orange, dried thyme and volcanic ash.
Nero d'Avola is deep in colour, soft and round, with mulberry and liquorice; Nerello Mascalese is pale and taut, with sour cherry, blood orange and high acidity.

cards.front: Nerello Mascalese: where is it at home, and how high do its vines climb?
cards.back: Mount Etna in Sicily, on terraces of black lava from about 400 to over 1,000 metres. Faro, above Messina, is a second home.

cards.front: Etna Rosso: what share of Nerello Mascalese, and which partner grape?
cards.back: At least 80 per cent Nerello Mascalese, with Nerello Cappuccio up to a fifth for colour and flesh. Etna became Sicily's first DOC in 1968.

cards.front: Nerello Mascalese: what has DNA shown of its parents, and whence its name?
cards.back: DNA work points to Sangiovese and Mantonico Bianco, a Calabrian white, as its parents. The name comes from Mascali, below Etna's eastern slope.

questions.q: A red poured blind is pale garnet, with sour cherry, blood orange and an ashy, smoky edge, high acidity and a fine, dusty tannin. It is Italian. Which grape is it?
questions.exp: Pale colour, blood orange and ash on high acidity and a fine, dusty tannin point to Nerello Mascalese. Nebbiolo, the nearest miss, is as pale but brings tar and a fiercer, drying grip.

questions.q: A guest asks what the word contrada means on a bottle of Etna Rosso. What do you tell her?
opts: A named district on one lava flow, like a cru
A wine aged four years before release
A wine made from old bush vines
A sparkling wine made in the bottle
questions.exp: A contrada is a named district on Etna's slopes, often one lava flow of one age, printed like a cru. Longer ageing is marked by Riserva, the nearest miss, not by contrada.

questions.q: A guest who loves red Burgundy wants an Italian red with the same pale colour and lift, and a volcanic edge. Which wine do you bring?
questions.exp: Etna Rosso, Nerello Mascalese from the slopes of Etna, is pale, high in acidity and ashy. Cerasuolo di Vittoria, the nearest miss, is light too but grows on red sand and is softer and fruitier.

report: Mode home, as the plan fixes it. Nothing contradicts TASTE.world old.

Etna DOC of 1968, Sicily's first, Etna Rosso at least 80 per cent Nerello Mascalese with Nerello Cappuccio to a fifth, the contrade as named districts on lava flows printed like crus, terraces from 400 to over 1,000 metres, old ungrafted bush vines, a harvest into late October and November, gentle extraction and large old casks, Rosato and a traditional method Spumante, Faro above Messina, and tuna, mushrooms and lamb all stand on the Codex's Sicily record; the pale colour, high acidity, firm dusty tannin, blood orange, rose and ash on GRAPES_PLUS.

The parentage (Sangiovese and Mantonico Bianco) stands on a peer reviewed paper of 2013 in Molecular Biotechnology, read through PubMed, and on Wine Grapes; the name from Mascali on two trade references. Calabria as its only other home on Gambero Rosso and a second trade page; cuttings sent to Australia are left out as unsettled.

TASTE gives body and alcohol as medium minus (body 1, alc 1). GRAPES_PLUS gives body medium, and Etna Rosso on a list is rarely light in alcohol, so the structure line says alcohol medium and body medium; a reviewer may wish to raise TASTE's alc to 2.

TASTE's acid is 2 (medium plus) where GRAPES_PLUS says high; the entry follows the reviewed profile, high. The Etna DOCG application of 2023 is left out, as the Codex's own record says no promotion had been published.
